summary: Teams of 2-4 students create a 3:00 to 5:00 minute multimedia promotional video spotlighting student athletes making a difference off the field. The video and required documentation are submitted online, and qualifying teams present their project virtually to judges. Entries must follow copyright, fair use, and AI citation guidelines.
time_limits: Setup: no more than three (3) minutes
Presentation: no more than ten (10) minutes
Judges’ questions: no more than five (5) minutes
submission_requirements: Submit one combined PDF file containing the URL to the Promotional Video, Works Cited, BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage and Documentation Form
Contestant ID is required for all submissions
Materials must follow BPA Graphic Standards and proper use of BPA logo and/or organization’s name
deadlines: Event registration deadline: no later than 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time, on December 1, 2026
National submission deadline: January 15, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time
competencies: Demonstrate proficiency in industry-standard video production software and equipment to execute all phases of the production process
Develop a cohesive storyline using a storyboard and script that applies effective scripting techniques to deliver a clear, focused message
Apply professional camera techniques, including intentional selection of shot types, angles, and framing to support visual storytelling
Implement lighting techniques, including proper setup and adjustment of light sources, to achieve consistent and professional visual quality
Perform non-linear editing using industry-standard tools, incorporating transitions, cuts, and audio editing techniques to produce a seamless and polished final cut
Apply titles, lower thirds, and 2D and/or 3D visual effects to enhance the final product and reinforce the intended message
Demonstrate an understanding of audience analysis by designing and delivering a final product that effectively communicates to a defined target audience

rubric.criterion: Team followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.
The promotional video adhered to the required time range of 3:00 –5:00 minutes, met the minimum resolution of 1920×1080 and conformed to BPA Graphic Standards.

Team submitted one (1) combined PDF file containing the URL to the Promotional Video, Works Cited (formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual), BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage and Documentation Form.

rubric.description: Layout is exceptionally well-organized; enhances comprehension and flow.

rubric.criterion: Aesthetic Use of Colors and Fonts
rubric.description: Colors and fonts are thoughtfully chosen; enhance visual appeal and readability.
Visuals strongly reinforce and elevate the theme and purpose.
Assets are high-quality and creatively used; design is professional and engaging.
Audio is crisp, well-balanced, and professionally mixed with no distractions.
Lighting is well-executed; effects enhance the visual experience and storytelling.
Motion graphics are skillfully integrated and enhance the visual narrative.
Production is original and imaginative, with bold creative choices that enhance its impact.
Color grading enhances tone and emotion; visual effects are polished, purposeful, and support the story.

rubric.criterion: Team followed Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

rubric.description: Demonstrates strong verbal and non-verbal communication with enthusiasm and effective virtual engagement.
The presentation content flows adequately, with a mostly clear structure and smooth transitions between points.
Thorough and insightful explanation of all project phases with clear rationale and reflection.
Media elements are creatively and effectively used to enhance the presentation; transitions and effects are smooth and professional.
Offers a detailed and insightful explanation of technology and software choices, including their impact on the project.
Responses are detailed, insightful, and effectively address the judges' questions.
At least two original team members were present during the presentation.
Setup lasted no longer than three (3) minutes, and the presentation lasted no more than ten (10) minutes.

judging_notes: Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level.
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC.
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring.
Presentation will be stopped at ten (10) minutes.
eligibility_notes: Any middle level, secondary or postsecondary contestant may enter this event.
A team will consist of 2 -4 contestants.
There are no restrictions on the number of entries per chapter or per state.
Teams who do not submit an entry following the topic listed below or do not follow the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines or Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy will be disqualified.
Contestants participating in the competition must be registered for the event prior to the submission deadline to be eligible.
Only the team captain should complete the submission.
